Write the reactant as:

\[
\mathrm{PhO{-}CH_2{-}C(CH_3)_2{-}CH{=}CH_2}
\]

HBr protonates the terminal alkene carbon, generating the more stable internal carbocation:

\[
\mathrm{PhO{-}CH_2{-}C(CH_3)_2{-}C^+H{-}CH_3}
\]

Instead of simply being captured by bromide, this cation can undergo intramolecular attack by the activated ortho position of the phenoxy ring:

1. **Direct cyclization:** Ortho attack on the original cation forms a six-membered oxygen-containing ring. Rearomatization gives **3,3,4-trimethylchromane**.

2. **Rearrangement followed by cyclization:** A Wagner–Meerwein 1,2-methyl shift converts the cation into

\[
\mathrm{PhO{-}CH_2{-}C^+(CH_3){-}CH(CH_3)_2}
\]

Ortho attack on this rearranged cation forms a five-membered ring, producing **3-isopropyl-3-methyl-2,3-dihydrobenzofuran**.

Thus the two TLC spots correspond to these two cationic cyclization pathways, not ordinary hydrobromination products.

Answer: B
